column3: In Spring MVC, and servlet applications in general, it is assumed that applications can block the current thread, for example for remote calls (`spring-fw-webflux-new-framework#webflux-concurrency-model`).
column5: In Spring MVC (and servlet applications in general), it is assumed that applications can block the current thread, (for example, for remote calls).

column3: For this reason, servlet containers use a large thread pool to absorb potential blocking during request handling (`spring-fw-webflux-new-framework#webflux-concurrency-model`).
column5: For this reason, servlet containers use a large thread pool to absorb potential blocking during request handling.

column3: In Spring WebFlux, and non-blocking servers in general, it is assumed that applications do not block (`spring-fw-webflux-new-framework#webflux-concurrency-model`).
column5: In Spring WebFlux (and non-blocking servers in general), it is assumed that applications do not block.

column3: Non-blocking servers use a small, fixed-size thread pool, called event loop workers, to handle requests (`spring-fw-webflux-new-framework#webflux-concurrency-model`).
column5: Therefore, non-blocking servers use a small, fixed-size thread pool (event loop workers) to handle requests.

column3: Never blocking the current thread and relying on callbacks means that you do not need extra threads, as there are no blocking calls to absorb (`spring-fw-webflux-new-framework#webflux-concurrency-model`).
column5: “To scale” and “small number of threads” may sound contradictory, but to never block the current thread (and rely on callbacks instead) means that you do not need extra threads, as there are no blocking calls to absorb.

column3: Reactive and non-blocking generally do not make applications run faster (`spring-fw-webflux-new-framework#webflux-performance`).
column5: Reactive and non-blocking generally do not make applications run faster.

column3: It requires more work to do things the non-blocking way, and that can slightly increase the required processing time (`spring-fw-webflux-new-framework#webflux-performance`).
column5: However, it requires more work to do things the non-blocking way, and that can slightly increase the required processing time.

column3: The key expected benefit of reactive and non-blocking is the ability to scale with a small, fixed number of threads and less memory (`spring-fw-webflux-new-framework#webflux-performance`).
column5: The key expected benefit of reactive and non-blocking is the ability to scale with a small, fixed number of threads and less memory.

column3: To observe those benefits, you need to have some latency, including a mix of slow and unpredictable network I/O (`spring-fw-webflux-new-framework#webflux-performance`).
